messages.subject: How can I make the SelectInput 'choices' change based on the loaded file's column headers?
parts:
I am graphing different time series signals, from many different .csv files.  These files all have different column headers, and I would like the choices for each input to change based on the column headers of each file.

Right now, I have all of my files stored in the workspace, so in ui.R, I was doing:

selectInput("dataSelection1", label = "Choose a File", 
                  choices = c(File1","File2", "File3","File4"))
selectInput("headerSelection1", label = "Choose a Header", 
                  choices = names(loadedFile))


And in server.R I had:

loadedFile <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataSelection1,
            "File1" = File1,
            "File2" = File2,
           "File3" = File3,
           "File4" = File4)
    })

Where File1-File4 were all loaded into my workspace.

This was giving me an error where "loadedFile" was not found.  Can anyone see where I can fix this?

Thank you!

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: How can I make the SelectInput 'choices' change based on the loaded file's column headers?
parts:
Create the select(ize) input in UI without any choices, then use
updateSelectInput() / updateSelectizeInput() in server.R to pass
choices to the select(ize) input.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: How can I make the SelectInput 'choices' change based on the loaded file's column headers?
parts:
Okay, a minimal example for you:

library(shiny)
shinyApp(
ui = fluidPage(
selectizeInput('foo', 'FOO', choices = NULL),
actionButton('update', 'Update')
),
server = function(input, output, session) {
observeEvent(input$update, {
updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = sample(letters, 10))
})
}
)

Please see if you are able to adapt it to your own app.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: How can I make the SelectInput 'choices' change based on the loaded file's column headers?
parts:
I wrote the minimal example just to show you the idea, and there is no
need to use action buttons at all. In your case, it is
input$dataSelection1 (instead of an action button) that triggers the
update of choices of the select input `dataSelection`.

observeEvent({
updateSelectizeInput(session, 'dataSelection', choices =

names(dataSource1()))
})

Note `dataSource1` is a reactive, and you must use it like a function,
i.e. don't forget the parentheses.

Regards,
Yihui

output$TempRise <- renderDygraph({
if (is.null(input$channel1)) return()
component <- File1[, input$channel1]

dygraph(component, main = "Data Graph") %>%
dyRangeSelector() %>%
dyOptions(colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))

})

Regards,
Yihui
